headline: High: Khoj’s broad read access plus xonsh’s shell/write defaults create dangerous shared-workspace and cascading-error pathways; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and can use optional web search; xonsh executes shell commands and reads/writes the filesystem. If Khoj ingests xonsh-produced files or command output as trusted content, prompt injection is plausible in default shared-workspace setups, though no direct shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes files that xonsh writes into the same workspace, injection becomes reachable.
IF xonsh output is copied into Khoj notes without sanitization, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable automatic indexing of xonsh-generated files.
Add a manual review step before Khoj ingests shell output.
Use read-only mounts for Khoj’s source corpus.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for indexed content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while xonsh can read filesystem contents and environment variables and write files. In a shared workspace, xonsh can expose data that Khoj later indexes or surfaces, creating a realistic leakage path even without explicit network exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem tree, xonsh can place sensitive files where Khoj indexes them.
IF Khoj indexes xonsh-created artifacts, private data can reappear in chat outputs.
mitigations: Keep Khoj’s index directory separate from xonsh workdirs.
Restrict xonsh to a least-privilege account.
Exclude secrets and env dumps from indexing.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj has read-only filesystem access but broad network egress; xonsh has shell execution, subprocess spawning, and filesystem write access. They do not both write the same state by profile, so the conflict is not high, but overlapping filesystem access can still race on shared files if the operator co-locates them.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, xonsh can overwrite files Khoj reads.
IF the operator shares a mutable cache or notebook folder, stale reads and clobbers can occur.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Make Khoj’s corpus read-only.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared notebooks.
Serialize access with a simple lock file.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can retrieve and summarize documents, and xonsh can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses. If xonsh treats Khoj’s retrieved text as authoritative, a mistaken summary can cascade into real command execution; the reverse direction is weaker, but the pair still forms a default inference-to-action chain.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes Khoj summaries without verification, incorrect facts can trigger commands.
IF Khoj surfaces stale or hallucinated notes into xonsh workflows, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human confirmation before execution.
Compare Khoj outputs against source documents.
Limit xonsh to dry-run mode for risky commands.
Log command provenance beside retrieved text.
requires-engineering: add structured verification between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly handles personal notes and indexed documents, while xonsh handles filesystem contents and environment variables. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is evident: sensitive local data could be exposed to a less-governed shell workflow, but not enough for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, xonsh may process it outside the intended governance boundary.
IF the operator routes personal notes into shell logs, retention controls may be bypassed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Disable shell history for sensitive sessions.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Use separate accounts for personal and regulated data.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries.
